rows.title: Arabic 1
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Demonstrate reading and listening comprehension of basic everyday materials related to oneself, family and immediate surroundings within a cultural context. These may include, but are not limited to, advertisements, time tables, short personal letters, dialogues, readings, conversations, and video and audio recordings.

Communicate, both orally and in writing, about familiar topics and activities requiring a simple and direct exchange of information within a cultural context. This communication may include, but is not limited to, simple verbal and written exchanges such as dialogues and paragraphs related to oneself, family and immediate surroundings.

Reflect on and evaluate similarities and differences in specific cultural practices and perspectives as related, but not limited to, greetings, education, family traditions, sports, leisure activities, cultural events and artistic expressions.
objectives: Comprehend standard spoken Arabic related to the individual and his/her surroundings, likes and dislikes, daily routine, leisure activities and past experiences with a recognition vocabulary of 1000 words.

Apply reading strategies in order to understand and analyze 150- to 200-word short articles, dialogues, stories and other authentic literary and factual texts related to the self, family and surroundings, written in Arabic alphabet.

Use acquired elementary vocabulary and grammar to communicate orally about emotional and mental states; the individual; school and work; origin and family; plans and needs; sports and cultural events with an active vocabulary of approximately 500 words.
Use targeted beginning-level grammar and vocabulary to compose 100- to 150-word paragraphs of connected discourse on personal, familiar and cultural topics, using Arabic alphabet.

Identify and use the indicative mood of regular, irregular, and stem-changing verbs in the simple present, present progressive, near future and preterite when engaged in receptive and communicative activities.

Recognize and apply gender and number agreement rules with definite and indefinite articles; descriptive, possessive and demonstrative adjectives; subject, reflexive, direct and indirect object, double object, and relative pronouns when using both receptive and expressive skills.
Understand and use imperative, declarative, negative and interrogative simple and compound sentences in oral and written activities.
Identify verbal and non-verbal differences between Arabic-speaking cultures and their own as related to greetings, leave-taking, and levels of formality.
Identify verbal and non-verbal differences between Arabic-speaking cultures and their own as related to education, family, daily life, traditions, holidays, and artistic expression.

rows.title: DC Electronics
rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Solve basic, direct current, electronic problems involving resistance, current, voltage, and power, as applied to both simple and complex combinations of series and/or parallel circuit components, comprised of resistors, capacitors and coils, in a given network configuration.
Diagram and discuss the relationship between electricity and magnetism as related to a DC permanent magnet motor, a solenoid or an electromechanical relay.
Describe and contrast the construction, operation, and purpose of resistors, potentiometers, switches, fuses, relays, and batteries.
objectives: Apply Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws, and other foundational electrical principles in the analysis of circuits.
Master the fundamentals of voltage, current, resistance, and power in DC circuits.
Utilize network theorems like Thevenin’s and Norton’s for simplifying and solving circuits.
Conduct experiments and interpret results with standard electrical measurement tools to verify theoretical predictions.

rows.title_printed: Course Outline: Riverside Community College District
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate the following skills:
outcomes: Explain the relationship between the cultural phenomenon of religion and the development of the category "religion" as variously defined in religious studies.
Compare and evaluate how religious traditions develop in particular contexts and cultures using the methods and tools presented in the course.

Examine the relationship between historical and contemporary varieties of religious experience and the cultures in which they are found.
Discuss the role of primary religious texts in their religious traditions through their respective interpretive frameworks.
Examine the relationship between religious traditions and political and social issues that arise in their respective cultures.
Recognize the influence of Christian European colonization on the development of religious studies as an academic field.
